body:
We've hit this bug.

We have our form's creation/destruction affected by an ngSwitch. If we use formControlName in our inputs, hiding and showing (creating and destroying) the form causes Subjects and SubjectSubscriptions to grow and never dispose.

It's been a hard time to debug this and memory leaks are always important.

I hope this gets fixed as soon as possible.

Thanks
We can provide a stackblitz project if needed.

We have run into this leak and it a pretty big deal - any ETA on when this might be fixed and available.

Anybody know of a workaround ?

Just ran into this bug. I have custom input with the NG_VALIDATORS provided. If user enters invalid data and navigates to the other tab of the same form, causing this custom input to be destroyed, he is unable to submit the form ever again without navigating out (force form to be destroyed). I think this bug is really severe.
I recently ran into this problem with a rather large project and its causing a major performance issue. Any updates here would put my mind at ease.

Why has such a critical issue been open for a year without being addressed? This is not just a memory leak, this makes it impossible to submit any form on our site after a user enters invalid input once. 

Has anyone discovered a workaround?
Workaround - do not use html attribute validators with formControlName and recreate FormGroup instance when big memory leak is possible

The plunker example is dead. Here is a minimized stackblitz version:
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-jr5cds?file=src%2Fapp%2Fcontrol.component.html

The workaround we can come up with for now is to use hidden attribute instead of ngIf for the snippet of form to enforce stabilized structure of the reactive formgroup.

body:
@longgt as explained by @devoto13 [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/22503#issuecomment-452021464) that may cause unexpected behavior. After digging a bit into the code I think I understood why:
- every FormControlDirective will create an instance of a FormControl
- if you create multiple FormControlDirective that have the same formControl or FormControlName they will refer to the same FormControl instance
- within your example, destroying one of those directive attached to a component would trigger the `_clearChangeFns` that will clear everything for all the others too

I agree that it might not be super common to have multiple FormControlDirective pointing to the same FormControl but still, just a warning :) 

A proper fix for that is doable but not trivial either...

body:
Unfortunately this is not just a memory leak. It can also corrupt form data and it has in our application. Let me show how:
 - Let's have a component with two instances of FormControl  stored in fields A and B and one input in component's view.
 - Now if we bind input with form control A and then change it to B everything works fine. Unless we update the value of control A. If we do, the input element will be updated with value of A but any change made to it by user will be saved in value of control B.
Here is a [StackBlitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-6aqeqc)
